subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 67-year-old woman reports a new unilateral temporal headache for 2 weeks, pain in her jaw when chewing, and tenderness when brushing her hair. She has noticed blurred vision in one eye. ESR is 85 mm/h and CRP is elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Giant cell (temporal) arteritis affects females older than 50 with unilateral headache, jaw claudication, temporal artery tenderness, and a risk of blindness from anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. It is a granulomatous vasculitis of the temporal, vertebral, and ophthalmic arteries with markedly elevated ESR/CRP, is associated with polymyalgia rheumatica, and is treated with high-dose glucocorticoids before biopsy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Takayasu arteritis affects Asian females younger than 40 with weak upper-extremity pulses and narrowing of the aortic arch and proximal great vessels.
explanation_incorrect.B: Migraine lacks jaw claudication, temporal tenderness, an elevated ESR, and a risk of blindness.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polyarteritis nodosa involves renal and visceral vessels, spares the lungs, and shows string-of-pearls microaneurysms with hepatitis B association.
explanation_incorrect.E: Buerger disease is a smoking-associated thrombosing vasculitis in young male smokers with claudication and gangrene.

educationalObjective: Giant cell arteritis presents in older women with headache, jaw claudication, temporal tenderness, high ESR, and a risk of blindness.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 70-year-old woman with visual symptoms and a temporal headache is suspected of having giant cell arteritis. A temporal artery biopsy is scheduled for next week.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?

options.text: Start high-dose glucocorticoids before the biopsy
Withhold glucocorticoids until the biopsy confirms the diagnosis
Perform an emergent temporal artery endarterectomy

explanation_correct: In giant cell arteritis, high-dose glucocorticoids should be started immediately, before temporal artery biopsy, because the major risk is irreversible blindness from anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. Biopsy can still demonstrate granulomatous inflammation after glucocorticoids have been begun.

explanation_incorrect.B: Withholding glucocorticoids risks irreversible vision loss; treatment should not wait for the biopsy result.
explanation_incorrect.C: Low-dose glucocorticoids are used for polymyalgia rheumatica; giant cell arteritis requires high-dose steroids.
explanation_incorrect.D: Endarterectomy is not a treatment for giant cell arteritis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Intravenous immunoglobulin is used for Kawasaki disease, not giant cell arteritis.

educationalObjective: Start high-dose glucocorticoids before temporal artery biopsy in giant cell arteritis to prevent irreversible blindness.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 28-year-old Asian woman has fatigue, fever, night sweats, and myalgias. Her blood pressure cannot be measured in either arm, and upper-extremity pulses are barely palpable. ESR is elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Takayasu arteritis, or 'pulseless disease,' affects Asian females younger than 40 with weak upper-extremity pulses, fever, night sweats, arthritis, and myalgias. It causes granulomatous thickening and narrowing of the aortic arch and proximal great vessels, with an elevated ESR, and is treated with glucocorticoids.

explanation_incorrect.A: Giant cell arteritis occurs in women older than 50 with temporal headache and jaw claudication.
explanation_incorrect.B: Polyarteritis nodosa affects middle-aged males with hepatitis B association, abdominal pain, and spares the lungs.
explanation_incorrect.C: Buerger disease is a thrombosing vasculitis in young male smokers with distal extremity ischemia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Kawasaki disease affects children younger than 4 with mucocutaneous findings and coronary artery aneurysms.

educationalObjective: Takayasu arteritis is a granulomatous large-vessel arteritis in young Asian women causing pulseless upper extremities and aortic arch narrowing.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 34-year-old man who smokes two packs of cigarettes daily has painful ischemic ulcers on his toes and intermittent claudication. He has Raynaud phenomenon and superficial nodular phlebitis, and has autoamputated one digit. Angiography shows segmental thrombosing lesions involving adjacent veins and nerves.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive treatment?
explanation_correct: Buerger disease (thromboangiitis obliterans) occurs in heavy-smoking males younger than 40 with claudication, gangrene, Raynaud phenomenon, autoamputation of digits, and superficial nodular phlebitis. It is a segmental thrombosing vasculitis involving veins and nerves, and the definitive treatment is smoking cessation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Glucocorticoids are used for giant cell arteritis and Takayasu arteritis, not Buerger disease.
explanation_incorrect.C: Intravenous immunoglobulin is the treatment for Kawasaki disease.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cyclophosphamide is used for severe ANCA-associated vasculitis and polyarteritis nodosa.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pyridostigmine is used to treat myasthenia gravis.

educationalObjective: Buerger disease is a segmental thrombosing vasculitis in young smokers, definitively treated by smoking cessation.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 3-year-old Asian child has had fever for 6 days along with bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, a polymorphous desquamating rash, cervical adenopathy, a strawberry tongue, and edema and erythema of the hands and feet.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Kawasaki disease affects Asian children younger than 4 with fever of at least 5 days plus the CRASH-and-burn criteria: bilateral nonexudative Conjunctivitis, polymorphous Rash with desquamation, cervical Adenopathy, Strawberry tongue, and Hand-foot changes. The major complication is coronary artery aneurysms, and treatment is intravenous immunoglobulin plus aspirin.

explanation_incorrect.A: IgA vasculitis follows an upper respiratory infection with palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs, arthralgias, and abdominal pain.
explanation_incorrect.B: Giant cell arteritis is a large-vessel arteritis in older women with headache and jaw claudication.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polyarteritis nodosa affects middle-aged males and spares the lungs.
explanation_incorrect.D: Microscopic polyangiitis is a pauci-immune necrotizing vasculitis with MPO-ANCA in adults.

educationalObjective: Kawasaki disease is a childhood vasculitis with fever of at least 5 days and CRASH-and-burn findings, complicated by coronary artery aneurysms and treated with IVIG and aspirin.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 52-year-old man has fever, weight loss, severe abdominal pain, melena, hypertension, and a mononeuritis multiplex. He is hepatitis B surface antigen positive. Angiography of the renal and mesenteric vessels shows multiple microaneurysms in a 'string of pearls' pattern, and the lungs are spared.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Polyarteritis nodosa affects middle-aged males, 30% of whom are hepatitis B positive, with fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, melena, hypertension, neurologic dysfunction, cutaneous eruptions, and renal damage. It involves renal and visceral vessels but spares the lungs, showing transmural inflammation with fibrinoid necrosis and string-of-pearls microaneurysms (skin, kidneys, intestines, nerves). Treatment is glucocorticoids and cyclophosphamide.

explanation_incorrect.A: Microscopic polyangiitis involves the lungs as well as kidneys and skin, is MPO-ANCA positive, and does not produce string-of-pearls microaneurysms.
explanation_incorrect.B: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis involves the upper and lower respiratory tract and kidneys with c-ANCA/PR3 and nasal septum perforation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis features asthma, eosinophilia, and neuropathy with elevated IgE.
explanation_incorrect.E: Buerger disease is a young smoker's thrombosing vasculitis without hepatitis B association or microaneurysms.

educationalObjective: Polyarteritis nodosa is a medium-vessel vasculitis in middle-aged men with hepatitis B, abdominal pain, hypertension, microaneurysms, and lung sparing.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 56-year-old woman has dyspnea, hemoptysis, palpable purpura on her lower extremities, and rapidly progressive renal failure. Kidney biopsy shows pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis. Serum testing is positive for MPO-ANCA (p-ANCA).
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Microscopic polyangiitis is a necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis involving the lungs, kidneys, and skin, with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis, palpable purpura, and MPO-ANCA (p-ANCA). It lacks the granulomatous inflammation and asthma or eosinophilia of the other ANCA-associated vasculitides, and is treated with cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids.

explanation_incorrect.B: Polyarteritis nodosa spares the lungs, is not ANCA-associated, and is linked to hepatitis B and microaneurysms.
explanation_incorrect.C: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis has asthma and eosinophilia with granulomas and elevated IgE.
explanation_incorrect.D: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis is c-ANCA/PR3 positive with upper respiratory involvement such as sinusitis and nasal septum perforation.
explanation_incorrect.E: IgA vasculitis is a childhood post-URI purpura with arthralgias and abdominal pain due to IgA deposition.

educationalObjective: Microscopic polyangiitis causes a pulmonary-renal syndrome with palpable purpura, pauci-immune glomerulonephritis, and MPO/p-ANCA positivity.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 45-year-old man with a long history of adult-onset asthma has worsening dyspnea, peripheral neuropathy, and weight loss. Laboratory studies show peripheral eosinophilia and an elevated IgE level. Biopsy shows granulomatous, necrotizing vasculitis with prominent eosinophilic infiltration.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, formerly Churg-Strauss syndrome, is defined by the combination of asthma, eosinophilia, and systemic vasculitis. Eosinophilic infiltration leads to inflammation and peripheral neuropathy, IgE is elevated, and histology shows a granulomatous, necrotizing vasculitis with eosinophilia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis features upper and lower respiratory and renal disease with c-ANCA and granulomas but not asthma and eosinophilia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Microscopic polyangiitis has pulmonary-renal pauci-immune glomerulonephritis without asthma or eosinophilia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polyarteritis nodosa spares the lungs and lacks eosinophilia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus, urticaria, and low C1q with anti-C1q antibodies.

educationalObjective: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss) is asthma plus eosinophilia plus systemic necrotizing vasculitis with peripheral neuropathy.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 49-year-old man has chronic sinusitis, otitis media, and a perforated nasal septum, followed by hemoptysis and dyspnea. Urinalysis shows red cell casts and rapidly progressive renal failure. Serology is positive for c-ANCA (PR3-ANCA).
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis has a triad of lung, vessel, and kidney involvement with upper respiratory disease (nasal septum perforation, chronic sinusitis, otitis media), lower respiratory findings such as hemoptysis, and pauci-immune rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. c-ANCA (PR3-ANCA) is positive, and treatment is glucocorticoids combined with rituximab or cyclophosphamide.

explanation_incorrect.A: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is dominated by asthma and eosinophilia rather than destructive upper respiratory disease.
explanation_incorrect.C: Microscopic polyangiitis lacks upper respiratory granulomatous destruction and is MPO/p-ANCA positive.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polyarteritis nodosa spares the lungs and lacks c-ANCA and sinusitis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is hepatitis C associated with purpura, weakness, arthralgias, and cryoglobulins.

educationalObjective: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis is upper and lower respiratory disease plus renal failure with c-ANCA/PR3 and nasal septum perforation.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 58-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis C has palpable purpura on her legs, weakness, and arthralgias. She also has peripheral neuropathy and glomerulonephritis. Testing reveals mixed IgG and IgM immune complexes that precipitate in the cold.
question: Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of her purpura?

options.text: Transmural fibrinoid necrosis of medium vessels with microaneurysms
IgA immune-complex deposition following a respiratory infection
Granulomatous inflammation and narrowing of the aortic arch
Mixed IgG and IgM immune complexes that precipitate in the cold

explanation_correct: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is often due to viral infections, especially hepatitis C, and causes a triad of palpable purpura, weakness, and arthralgias, with peripheral neuropathy and glomerulonephritis. Mixed IgG and IgM immune complexes precipitate in the cold and deposit in small vessels, producing an immune complex mediated, type III hypersensitivity vasculitis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with MPO-ANCA occurs in microscopic polyangiitis, not cryoglobulinemia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Transmural fibrinoid necrosis with string-of-pearls microaneurysms is characteristic of polyarteritis nodosa.
explanation_incorrect.C: Post-respiratory-infection IgA deposition is IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura).
explanation_incorrect.D: Granulomatous thickening and narrowing of the aortic arch is Takayasu arteritis.

educationalObjective: Hepatitis C associated mixed cryoglobulinemia causes purpura, weakness, and arthralgias from cold-precipitating IgG/IgM immune complexes.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 6-year-old boy develops palpable purpura on his buttocks and legs, arthralgias of the knees and ankles, and severe abdominal pain 10 days after an upper respiratory infection. Ultrasound demonstrates an intussusception.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: IgA vasculitis, formerly Henoch-Schonlein purpura, is the most common childhood vasculitis and often follows an upper respiratory infection due to IgA immune complex deposition. Its classic triad is arthralgias ('hinge' pain), abdominal pain that may reflect intussusception, and palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs; it is associated with IgA nephropathy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis is confined to the skin with no visceral involvement and occurs 7–10 days after drugs or infection.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus, urticaria, and low C1q with anti-C1q antibodies.
explanation_incorrect.D: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is hepatitis C related, typically affects adults, and involves cryoglobulins.
explanation_incorrect.E: Kawasaki disease has fever of at least 5 days, CRASH-and-burn findings, and coronary artery aneurysms.

educationalObjective: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura) is a childhood post-URI vasculitis with palpable purpura, arthralgias, abdominal pain, and possible intussusception.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 24-year-old man of Turkish descent has had recurrent painful oral ulcers and genital ulcers for the past year. He also has episodes of uveitis and tender erythematous nodules on his shins. Testing is positive for HLA-B51.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Behcet syndrome is an all-vessel vasculitis with increased incidence in patients of Turkish and Eastern Mediterranean descent, characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis, and erythema nodosum. Flares last 1–4 weeks, it may be triggered by herpes simplex virus or parvovirus, and it is associated with HLA-B51.

explanation_incorrect.B: Giant cell arteritis is a large-vessel arteritis in older women with headache and jaw claudication.
explanation_incorrect.C: IgA vasculitis is a childhood purpuric rash with arthralgias and abdominal pain following an upper respiratory infection.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polyarteritis nodosa is a visceral medium-vessel vasculitis in middle-aged men with hepatitis B and microaneurysms.
explanation_incorrect.E: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis features asthma, eosinophilia, and peripheral neuropathy.

educationalObjective: Behcet syndrome is an all-vessel vasculitis with recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis, erythema nodosum, and HLA-B51 association.
